name: Vertiv
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Vertiv is the pure-play benchmark for AI data-center power and cooling — roughly three-quarters or more of revenue is data-center, backlog reached $15.0B at end-2025 (+109% year over year, book-to-bill ~2.9x in Q4), and Dell'Oro ranks it in a statistical tie with Schneider Electric for #1 in global data-center physical infrastructure. The Q2 2026 print cracked the streak: a ~$100M revenue miss on supply-chain and project-timing issues cut the stock ~10-17% in a day despite raised guidance. BACKGROUND: Heritage dates to 1965 (Liebert, the pioneer of computer-room cooling); spun through Emerson Network Power to the Vertiv name in 2016; NYSE-listed 2020; ~34,000 employees, 130+ countries, executive chairman David Cote (ex-Honeywell), CEO Giordano Albertazzi. FY2025 revenue $10.2B (+27.7%). Named NVIDIA 800 VDC data-center power systems partner; full 800 VDC portfolio scheduled for 2H 2026.
ecosystemRole: We assess Vertiv as the scale-and-win-rate yardstick every other power/cooling vendor in this file is measured against, and the cleanest public proxy for AI data-center capex sentiment. Basis: the highest data-center revenue concentration among large-caps (~75-80%), a top-share position in both power (top-5 with Schneider/ABB/Eaton/Delta) and thermal (Omdia top-3, ~6 points of share gained), and a stock that moves violently on AI-demand news (the DeepSeek scare cut it ~25-30% in days). For challengers like Megmeet and Sinexcel, Vertiv defines the incumbent product benchmark; for the 800 VDC transition, it is the incumbent with the most centralized-UPS content at risk and the most aggressive replacement roadmap.

productsAndServices.name: Critical power (Trinergy UPS, PowerDirect Rack, DC power)
productsAndServices.description: Trinergy is the flagship AI-class large UPS: 1,500-2,500 kVA blocks scalable to 20 MW, transformer-free IGBT double conversion, >=97% VFI efficiency (>=99% in Dynamic Online Mode), pitched explicitly at fluctuating AI loads. PowerDirect Rack (March 2025) is an OCP ORv3-compliant 50V DC power shelf covering 33-132 kW per rack with N+N redundancy, AC and HVDC input compatible. Plus switchgear, busway, static transfer switches, and power distribution.
productsAndServices.positioning: Top-5 global in data-center power and UPS; the Trinergy-class large-UPS franchise is exactly the content the 800 VDC architecture threatens, making the DC-rack portfolio the hedge.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct and channel with heavy services attach (4,000+ field service engineers).
productsAndServices.roadmap: Full 800 VDC ecosystem — centralized rectifiers, DC busway, rack DC-DC converters, DC-compatible backup — releases 2H 2026, ahead of NVIDIA Kyber/Rubin Ultra (2027).

productsAndServices.name: Thermal management & liquid cooling (CoolChip CDUs, CoolLoop, chillers)
productsAndServices.description: CoolChip CDU family spans 70 kW to 2,300 kW (in-rack, in-row, perimeter; liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air) for direct-to-chip cooling; CoolLoop RDHx rear-door heat exchangers to 80 kW; free-cooling and Liebert AFC chillers; BiXin magnetic-bearing centrifugal chiller technology acquired 2024. Omdia ranks Vertiv top-3 in data-center thermal with share gains.
productsAndServices.positioning: The liquid-cooling M&A race centers on Vertiv (PurgeRite ~$1.0B fluid services, Strategic Thermal Labs, ThermoKey, BMarko) versus Eaton's $9.5B Boyd buy and Schneider's Motivair — Vertiv assembled equivalent scope in smaller pieces.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, OEM channels (ThermoKey), and services contracts including fluid commissioning (PurgeRite NearZero).
productsAndServices.roadmap: GB300 NVL72 reference architecture (142 kW/rack) shipping; capacity doubling at the Italian chiller campus by end-2026.

productsAndServices.name: Prefabricated infrastructure (OneCore, SmartRun)
productsAndServices.description: OneCore (August 2025): factory-assembled prefabricated data centers in 5-50 MW single blocks, 96-944 racks, integrating Trinergy UPS, CoolChip CDUs, and chillers under the Unify management platform. SmartRun (March 2025): modular overhead prefab integrating busbar, liquid-cooling piping, and containment — installs at roughly 1 MW+ per day, up to 85% faster than stick-build.
productsAndServices.positioning: Direct competitor to Eaton's Fibrebond/Flexnode stack and Schneider's EcoStruxure pods; four new/expanded Americas plants (two new South Carolina sites, ~7x infrastructure-solutions capacity when ramped) back the bet.
targetSegments: Enterprise, colo, sovereign, neocloud data centers
productsAndServices.roadmap: BMarko acquisition (April 2026) adds structural fabrication capacity for modular builds.

productsAndServices.name: Energy storage (DynaFlex BESS, EnergyCore Grid)
productsAndServices.description: DynaFlex BESS: modular lithium (LFP) systems, 1.5-6 MW class, UL9540A-tested, 2 ms PCS response — peak shaving, demand management, diesel-generator replacement, hybrid power. EnergyCore Grid (December 2025, North America): utility-grade BESS scaling 1 MW to 200+ MW with integrated PCS and EMS, aimed at accelerating data-center grid interconnection, ancillary services, and black start.
productsAndServices.positioning: Puts Vertiv directly into the utility-scale BESS integrator space occupied by Fluence, Tesla, and Sungrow — but sold through the data-center relationship rather than the IPP channel.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to data-center operators and their energy partners.
productsAndServices.roadmap: EnergyCore Grid is the newest product line — deployment evidence is the thing to watch through 2026.

productsAndServices.name: Monitoring, management & services (Unify, Avocent, 4,000+ field engineers)
productsAndServices.description: Unify consolidates real-time power/thermal management; Avocent embedded management, KVM, and serial consoles; Waylay NV acquisition (August 2025) adds generative-AI operational intelligence. Services span project, liquid-cooling and fluid management, UPS/battery, switchgear/busway, and digital services.
productsAndServices.positioning: The services moat: recurring revenue and installed-base lock-in that pure hardware challengers lack.
productsAndServices.roadmap: AI-driven operational intelligence (Waylay) folding into Unify.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Vertiv functions as the sector's leveraged proxy: its equity and orders amplify AI-capex sentiment in both directions. Basis: +14-20% on the Q4 2025 order blowout, -25-30% in days on the DeepSeek scare, -10-17% on a 3% revenue miss — against a business whose backlog ($15B) and book-to-bill (~2.9x) kept strengthening throughout.

(High confidence) We assess the #1 position is real but shared and contested. Basis: Dell'Oro places Schneider and Vertiv ~0.1 point apart at the top of data-center physical infrastructure; hyperscalers are deliberately multi-sourcing (Aaon and Modine ramping thermal, Eaton buying Boyd), and Delta-class ODM power vendors sit closer to the NVIDIA rack than any incumbent.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the 800 VDC transition is a net-content question Vertiv has not yet proven. Basis: independent analysis (SemiAnalysis) projects the architecture contracts the centralized UPS market — a core Vertiv franchise — while creating ~$11B power-rack and ~$13B solid-state-transformer markets; Vertiv's 2H 2026 DC portfolio is announced but no incumbent has yet named a shipping 800 VDC switchboard product.

(Moderate confidence) We assess execution, not demand, is the binding risk into 2027. Basis: the Q2 2026 revenue miss on supply-chain/project timing, five simultaneous plant expansions, five acquisitions integrating (Great Lakes, Waylay, PurgeRite, ThermoKey, BMarko, Strategic Thermal Labs), and the 2021-22 precedent — management underestimated inflation, produced a 37% one-day drop, and drew securities litigation that still defines the bear case's execution argument.

(Moderate confidence) We assess EnergyCore Grid signals convergence between data-center power vendors and the BESS integrator space. Basis: a 1 MW-200+ MW utility-grade product sold through data-center relationships attacks the interconnection-queue problem that Fluence/Tesla-class integrators serve from the IPP side — a lane-crossing move worth tracking for every storage vendor in this file.

relationships.context: Vertiv is a named NVIDIA 800 VDC data-center power systems partner: platform designs advanced to engineering readiness (October 2025) with early design engagement on multiple gigawatt-scale AI-factory projects, timed for Kyber/Rubin Ultra in 2027; an energy-efficient cooling + power reference architecture for GB300 NVL72 (142 kW/rack) with SimReady assets in Omniverse (June 2025); and a DGX GB300 federal deployment at the Naval Postgraduate School (July 2026).

relationships.note: Statistical tie for #1 in global data-center physical infrastructure (Dell'Oro).
relationships.context: Dell'Oro ranks Vertiv and Schneider ~0.1 point apart at the top of data-center physical infrastructure. Vertiv is the pure-play (~75-80% data-center revenue, backlog $15.0B at end-2025, +109% YoY) against Schneider's diversified portfolio — and the two run parallel reference-design franchises, liquid-cooling M&A programs, and US prefab-capacity buildouts.

relationships.note: Liquid-cooling M&A rival ($9.5B Boyd vs Vertiv's four-deal assembly) and prefab competitor.
relationships.context: Eaton's $9.5B Boyd acquisition bought in one stroke the liquid-cooling scope Vertiv assembled through PurgeRite (~$1.0B), Strategic Thermal Labs, ThermoKey and BMarko; Eaton's Fibrebond/Flexnode stack competes with Vertiv OneCore/SmartRun in prefab, backed on Vertiv's side by four new/expanded Americas plants (~7x infrastructure-solutions capacity when ramped).

relationships.note: Vertiv's DynaFlex/EnergyCore Grid enters the utility-scale BESS integrator space from the data-center side.
relationships.context: EnergyCore Grid (1 MW-200+ MW utility-grade BESS sold through data-center relationships) puts Vertiv directly into the integrator space occupied by Fluence, Tesla and Sungrow — attacking the interconnection-queue problem from the data-center channel rather than the IPP channel. The lane-crossing move the dossier flags for every storage vendor.

relationships.note: Rack-level challenger in the shelf/BBU territory Vertiv is moving down into.
relationships.context: Vertiv's PowerDirect Rack (ORv3 50V DC shelf) entry moves it down into the shelf/BBU territory where Delta, LITEON and Megmeet operate — while for challengers like Megmeet and Sinexcel, Vertiv defines the incumbent product benchmark, with the most centralized-UPS content at risk in the 800 VDC transition and the most aggressive replacement roadmap.
